evidence.note: Repeated full-suite runs (bash /app/run_tests.sh) followed by long stdin key sequences scrolling interactive output — coarse feedback, the baseline harness.

Runs the compiler on individual specific failing test files to isolate behavior, then re-runs the same files after patching to confirm the fix before scaling to the full suite — a real per-test debug loop.
Inspects expected assembly files (data_on_page_boundary_linux.s) to compare against, an element of anchor-8 assembly inspection.
Reads the specific failing test source files to understand what construct is failing, isolating the debugging target rather than blind recompiling.
Patch → rebuild → re-run the isolated test cycle, showing fixes validated at per-test granularity before the full run.

reasoning: The agent goes beyond only running the full suite: it isolates failing tests, runs them individually, reads their sources, inspects expected assembly, and re-validates the specific case after each patch before re-running the whole suite — matching anchor 5 fully and partially reaching anchor 8's assembly-inspection and per-feature slicing. It falls short of 8 because there are no hand-crafted minimal reproductions, no systematic emitted-asm diffing or root-cause categorization, and the verification breadth is a handful of existing test files with much reliance on the slow interactive full run. This places it at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.
